description: Valtuutus is a high-performance Relationship-Based Access Control (ReBAC) authorization library for .NET inspired by Google Zanzibar, for fine-grained permissions in ASP.NET Core and .NET applications.
releaseNotes:
This release adds OpenTelemetry traces and metrics built around how the engines run a request: per call, per database round trip, per write. It also fixes a stale cached allow after a revoke, and removes two query plans that could cost tens of milliseconds on skewed or large data.

## Changes that need action

* **Write/delete notifications run after commit** (#334).  used to run inside the write's transaction, before the commit. With caching, a tokenless check landing in that window could cache the pre-commit answer for 5 minutes; after a revoke, that answer was allowed.
  * Overloads that commit their own transaction now run the handlers after .
  * Overloads that take **your** transaction no longer run them. Call  on the writer after you commit.  shows the pattern.
  *  is now a list: use  instead of assigning it. Handlers run in the order added, so  and your own handlers no longer replace each other.
* **Telemetry contract** (#335). The spans emitted until now followed the removed V1 engines, and  emitted no span at all since 2.0. They are replaced:
  * span names changed (below);
  * the request-object tags (, , ...) and the  /  events are gone;
  * the  and per-provider-method span names are gone;
  *  and  are removed; nothing was emitted on that source.

  Update any dashboards, alerts or trace queries that match on the old names.

## New: traces

Subscribe with . See [Telemetry](https://github.com/valtuutus/valtuutus/blob/main/Telemetry.md).

* , , ,  and : one span per engine call. Attributes:
  * entity and subject types and ids, and the permission;
  * the snap token, and whether it came from the request or was resolved;
  * the result, the number of round trips and the number of lookup steps;
  * error status on failure.
* : one per database round trip. Attributes: the queries it ran, whether it resolved the snap token, the lookup step, , and  when the engine had already answered (short-circuited work).
*  / : one per write or delete, covering the commit when Valtuutus owns the transaction.
* : one per cached call, with the hit flag.

## New: metrics

Subscribe with . Metrics carry no ids, entity types or permissions.

| Instrument | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
|  (s) | histogram | operation, snap token source, result (check, explain), cache hit,  |
|  | histogram | same |
|  | counter | operation, snap token source, cache hit |
|  (s) | histogram | write/delete,  |
|  | counter | relation/attribute |

* Each call is measured once, where the caller waits for it. With caching, cache hits are included.
* On .NET 9+ the duration histograms suggest buckets from 0.1 ms to 2.5 s. On .NET 8, add the  shown in ; otherwise every call lands in the first bucket.

## Fixes and performance

* **Skewed usersets no longer scan every tuple** (#332). Userset joins, the TTU fast path and fused TTU leaves now pick the 2-hop join's direction per execution. Checks on an entity with 50k userset tuples went from 61 ms to ~0.13 ms on Postgres, and from 78 ms to ~0.28 ms on SQL Server.
  * New option  (default 32) on  and .
  * Cost on ordinary checks: about +5 µs per two-hop executed on Postgres; SQL Server is within noise except  (178 → 211 µs).
* **Postgres single-entity attribute reads seek by entity id** (#333). They used a catch-all statement that, under a generic plan, scanned every attribute of the entity type (0.69 ms vs 0.016 ms on 10k attributes).
* **InMemory publishes its latest token after applying the data** (#334).
* **Telemetry cost with nothing listening:** no new allocations. Time is +3.5% (~70 ns) at worst on InMemory microbenchmarks, and well under 0.1% of a database round trip.

## Pull requests

* #332 perf(data): pick the two-hop userset join direction per execution
* #333 fix(postgres): seek single-entity attribute reads by entity id
* #334 fix(data)!: announce writes and deletes only after they commit
* #335 feat(telemetry): trace engine calls and their round trips (includes #336, metrics)
